title: Speech Pathologist Salary: Award Rates, Fortnightly Pay, and Annual Earnings
description: Learn how to calculate your speech pathologist salary from hourly award rates. Includes 38-hour week, fortnightly pay, tax, super, and casual loading.

Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an extra payment into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Speech Pathologist Salary

If you are a speech pathologist in Australia, your pay is likely covered by the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020**. This award sets minimum hourly rates for health professional employees, including speech pathologists, based on their qualifications and years of experience. The most common entry point is **Level 1, AQF Level 5, 1st year**, which pays **$32.44 per hour** as of the first full pay period starting on or after 1 October 2026.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

To estimate your annual speech pathologist salary, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee, the award defines ordinary hours as an average of 38 per week. So for a Level 1 speech pathologist:

$32.44 × 38 × 52 = **$64,108 per year**

This calculation assumes you work the same 38-hour week every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Most employers pay weekly or fortnightly. Your weekly pay before tax is:

$32.44 × 38 = **$1,232.72**

Fortnightly, that is **$2,465.44** (weekly × 2). This is useful for budgeting if you are paid on a fortnightly cycle.

### Casual Loading

If you are employed as a casual speech pathologist, you receive a **25% loading** on top of the minimum hourly rate. The casual rate for Level 1 (1st year) is:

$32.44 × 1.25 = **$40.55 per hour**

This loading is paid instead of entitlements like annual leave, personal leave, and public holidays. Casual employees also get overtime rates calculated on the loaded rate. For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Comparing Award Rates to the National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 per hour for casuals including loading. Award rates for speech pathologists are higher because they reflect the skilled nature of the profession. The Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission set these rates through annual wage reviews. Always use the award rate that matches your classification and experience level.

### Tax on Your Speech Pathologist Salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus a **2% Medicare levy** (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

For a $64,108 annual salary:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 (to $45,000): $4,020
- Tax on remaining $19,108 (to $64,108): $5,732
- Total tax: $9,752
- Medicare levy (2% of $64,108): $1,282
- **Total tax + Medicare: $11,034**

Your take-home pay would be approximately **$53,074 per year**, or **$1,020 per week**. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay **superannuation guarantee** at **12%** of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For a full-time speech pathologist:

$64,108 × 12% = **$7,693 per year**

Super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. If you earn above that, the 12% only applies up to that limit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: do **not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading – use the checkbox to add it automatically.

### Other Award Classifications

Speech pathologists with more experience or higher qualifications move up the pay scale. For example:

- Level 1, AQF Level 5, 2nd–3rd year: $34.44/hour → $68,045 annual
- Level 1, AQF Level 5, 4th–6th year: $37.53/hour → $74,159 annual
- Level 1, AQF Level 5, 7th year+: $40.56/hour → $80,147 annual

These rates are from the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guide and the Modern Awards Pay Database.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more award-specific pay guides, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. For reference tables of all classifications, see our [reference tables](/data).
